description: docs/verifications/compare_distributions.py evaluates every case with phit, R, and SciPy and compares each with mpmath references at 60 digits, rounded once to double. Case status is the largest relative error against the case's rule.

known_differences: For a point mass, the discrete quantile at p = 1 is the mass location; R and SciPy may return the upper support bound.
R's F density at +INF is NAN; phit returns 0.
R F quantiles can round to zero for tiny probabilities and small numerator df.
R's Student-t quantile at df = 0.5 has a small nonzero center and some far-tail inaccuracy.
R's discrete-quantile adjustment near 1 − 2^-52 can shift the count; phit uses a relative 64·EPSILON allowance on the smaller tail.
R's mean-form negative binomial mass differs from the high-precision value when size is much larger than the count.
SciPy's large-df chi-square CDF has about 8e-9 relative error at the saved lower-tail point.
